title: Dieter Rams' 10 Principles of Good Design
description: Dieter Rams' ten principles for good design, developed during his tenure as chief design officer at Braun. These timeless principles emphasize simplicity, honesty, and functionality that transcend aesthetics to define fundamental design quality.
author: Dieter Rams
context: Originally formulated for industrial design, these principles have become foundational for all design disciplines including digital product design, user interface design, and user experience design.

principles.name: Good design is innovative
principles.short_description: Innovation and technology are constantly advancing, creating new opportunities for innovative design that develop alongside them.
principles.detailed_description: Good design does not simply imitate existing forms. It harnesses technological possibilities and advances alongside them. Innovation is not about novelty for its own sake, but about finding genuinely better solutions to user needs. It requires understanding what is truly new and meaningful versus what is merely fashionable or different.
key_principles: Leverage new technological possibilities meaningfully
Find genuinely better solutions, not just different ones
Innovation serves user needs, not novelty for its own sake
Advance design thinking alongside technological progress
Question existing solutions and seek improvements

questions: Does the design leverage current technology in meaningful ways?
Does it solve problems in genuinely new or better ways?
Is innovation purposeful rather than arbitrary?
Does it advance user experience beyond existing solutions?
Has the design questioned assumptions and found better approaches?
what_to_look_for: Meaningful use of new technologies or approaches
Solutions that genuinely improve on existing patterns
Innovation that serves user needs, not designer ego
Purposeful departure from convention with clear benefits

common_violations.example: Reinventing standard UI patterns without clear benefit, confusing users
common_violations.impact: Users must relearn familiar interactions without gaining value

common_violations.example: Building interfaces that don't leverage modern capabilities like touch, voice, or AI when appropriate
common_violations.impact: Missed opportunities to genuinely improve user experience

common_violations.example: Copying competitor designs without considering if they're actually optimal
common_violations.impact: Perpetuates suboptimal patterns instead of finding better solutions

common_violations.example: Adding features simply because the technology exists, not because users need them
common_violations.impact: Complexity without corresponding user benefit

best_practices: Understand emerging technologies and their genuine user benefits
Question existing design patterns and test if improvements are possible
Innovate with clear purpose tied to user needs
Balance familiarity with meaningful advancement
Test innovative approaches to ensure they improve rather than complicate
Look for opportunities where new technology can solve old problems
Distinguish between meaningful innovation and superficial novelty

principles.name: Good design makes a product useful
principles.original_german: Gutes Design macht ein Produkt brauchbar
principles.short_description: A product is bought to be used. It must satisfy not only functional but also psychological and aesthetic criteria.
principles.detailed_description: The primary purpose of design is to optimize a product's utility. Good design emphasizes usefulness while disregarding anything that detracts from it. Design must fulfill both practical functionality and the psychological needs of users - products must work well and feel right to use.
key_principles: Optimize utility above all else
Satisfy both functional and psychological needs
Remove anything that detracts from usefulness
Ensure products work well in actual use
Balance practical function with emotional satisfaction

questions: Does the design fulfill its primary purpose effectively?
Are functional requirements met comprehensively?
Does the design satisfy users' psychological needs?
Is anything present that detracts from utility?
Does the product work well in real-world use scenarios?
what_to_look_for: Clear primary functionality that serves user needs
Absence of elements that impede utility
Features that support rather than distract from core purpose

common_violations.example: Beautiful interface that sacrifices usability for aesthetics
common_violations.impact: Users struggle to accomplish tasks despite visual appeal

common_violations.example: Adding many features that most users don't need, complicating the core experience
common_violations.impact: Core functionality becomes harder to access and use

common_violations.example: Designing for ideal conditions rather than real-world use scenarios
common_violations.impact: Product fails when used in actual environments

common_violations.example: Technically functional but unsatisfying or frustrating to use
common_violations.impact: Users can complete tasks but derive no satisfaction from the experience

best_practices: Prioritize core functionality above all other considerations
Understand and design for real-world use contexts
Test usefulness with actual users in realistic scenarios
Consider both task completion and user satisfaction
Remove features and elements that don't serve clear user needs
Ensure psychological comfort and satisfaction during use
Make primary tasks effortless and efficient

principles.name: Good design is aesthetic
principles.short_description: The aesthetic quality of a product is integral to its usefulness because products are used every day and have an effect on people and their well-being.
principles.detailed_description: Well-designed products are not only functional but beautiful. Aesthetic quality affects users' well-being and the products we use daily impact our person and our mood. However, only well-executed objects can be beautiful - aesthetics must be grounded in quality execution, not superficial decoration.
key_principles: Aesthetics are integral to usefulness, not separate
Beauty affects user well-being and experience
Aesthetic quality must be grounded in execution excellence
Visual quality reflects and supports functional quality
Beauty emerges from restraint and precision, not decoration

Does the aesthetic support rather than conflict with function?
Is the visual quality consistent with execution quality?
Does the aesthetic contribute to user well-being?
Is beauty achieved through restraint and precision?
what_to_look_for: Aesthetics that enhance rather than distract from function
Quality execution in all visual details
Aesthetics that age well and remain pleasing over time

common_violations.impact: Visual clutter that distracts from content and purpose

common_violations.impact: Design ages poorly and requires frequent visual overhauls

common_violations.example: Sacrificing readability or usability for visual effect

principles.name: Good design makes a product understandable
principles.original_german: Gutes Design macht ein Produkt verständlich
principles.short_description: It clarifies the product's structure. Better still, it can make the product clearly express its function by making use of the user's intuition.
principles.detailed_description: Good design makes a product self-explanatory. It clarifies structure and function intuitively, leveraging users' existing knowledge and intuition. At best, the product explains itself without requiring instructions - its purpose and operation are immediately apparent through its design.
key_principles: Make structure and function self-evident
Leverage user intuition and existing knowledge
Product should explain itself without instructions
Clarify rather than complicate
Use design to communicate purpose and operation

questions: Can users understand what the product does without explanation?
Is the structure and organization immediately apparent?
Does the design leverage intuitive patterns and expectations?
Can users operate the product without instructions?
Does the design clarify rather than mystify function?
what_to_look_for: Clear communication of purpose and capabilities
Minimal need for labels or instructions
Leverage of familiar patterns and mental models

common_violations.example: Icon-only buttons without clear meaning, requiring users to guess
common_violations.impact: Users cannot discover or understand functionality

common_violations.example: Important features accessible only through obscure gestures or shortcuts
common_violations.impact: Users never discover key capabilities

common_violations.example: Navigation and organization that don't match user mental models

principles.name: Good design is unobtrusive
principles.short_description: Products fulfilling a purpose are like tools. They are neither decorative objects nor works of art. Their design should therefore be both neutral and restrained, to leave room for the user's self-expression.
principles.detailed_description: Good design steps back and lets users focus on their tasks and goals. Products are tools that serve users, not objects that demand attention for themselves. Design should be neutral and restrained, allowing the user's content, work, and self-expression to take center stage. The design facilitates without intruding.

Products are tools, not decorative objects
Be neutral and restrained in approach
Allow user content and expression to dominate
Facilitate without demanding attention

common_violations.example: Unique, artistic interfaces that prioritize designer vision over usability

common_violations.example: Heavy branding elements that compete with user content

principles.name: Good design is honest
principles.short_description: It does not make a product appear more innovative, powerful or valuable than it really is. It does not attempt to manipulate the consumer with promises that cannot be kept.
principles.detailed_description: Good design is truthful and doesn't make false promises. It doesn't try to manipulate users by appearing more innovative, powerful, or valuable than it actually is. Honest design sets accurate expectations and delivers on them. It respects users by representing capabilities and limitations truthfully.
key_principles: Represent capabilities accurately and truthfully
Don't manipulate users with false promises
Set realistic expectations that will be met
Be transparent about limitations and tradeoffs
Respect users through honesty

Does the design avoid manipulative patterns?
Are users respected with truthful communication?
what_to_look_for: Accurate representation of features and capabilities
Realistic promises that are delivered upon
Absence of deceptive patterns and dark patterns
Consistency between marketing and actual experience

common_violations.example: Making cancellation difficult while making signup easy, hiding costs until late
common_violations.impact: Users feel manipulated and lose trust

common_violations.example: Marketing features that don't work well or don't exist
common_violations.impact: User disappointment and lost credibility

common_violations.example: Not disclosing important constraints or requirements until after commitment
common_violations.impact: Users make decisions based on incomplete information

common_violations.example: Fake progress bars or inflated metrics to appear more capable
common_violations.impact: False sense of progress and eventual user frustration

best_practices: Represent features and capabilities accurately in all communication
Be transparent about limitations, costs, and tradeoffs upfront
Avoid dark patterns and manipulative design techniques
Set conservative expectations and overdeliver rather than overpromise
Make important information visible before users commit
Ensure consistency between marketing and actual product experience
Respect user autonomy and decision-making with complete information

principles.name: Good design is long-lasting
principles.short_description: It avoids being fashionable and therefore never appears antiquated. Unlike fashionable design, it lasts many years even in today's throwaway society.
principles.detailed_description: Good design transcends fashion and trends. It is timeless rather than trendy, remaining relevant and effective for years. By avoiding stylistic fads and focusing on fundamental quality, good design doesn't become outdated or appear antiquated. This principle values longevity and sustainability over novelty.

Focus on timeless fundamentals over stylistic fads
Design for long-term relevance and effectiveness

Focus on fundamental usability over fashionable patterns
Design choices based on enduring principles
Avoidance of elements that will feel dated quickly

common_violations.impact: Design quickly feels outdated and requires frequent redesigns

common_violations.example: Adding trendy features (blockchain, NFTs) without genuine user value
common_violations.impact: Features become irrelevant as trends fade

Avoid stylistic trends that will date the design

principles.name: Good design is thorough down to the last detail
principles.original_german: Gutes Design ist konsequent bis ins letzte Detail
principles.short_description: Nothing must be arbitrary or left to chance. Care and accuracy in the design process show respect for the user.
principles.detailed_description: Good design is meticulous and deliberate. Nothing is left to chance or treated arbitrarily. Every detail is considered and executed with care and precision. This thoroughness demonstrates respect for users and contributes to overall quality. Attention to detail distinguishes good design from adequate design.

Nothing should be arbitrary or accidental
Care and precision demonstrate respect for users
Thoroughness contributes to overall quality perception

Refine micro-interactions and transitions with care
Use consistent spacing, sizing, and styling throughout

Treat every detail as important, from error messages to loading states

principles.name: Good design is environmentally friendly
principles.short_description: Design makes an important contribution to the preservation of the environment. It conserves resources and minimizes physical and visual pollution throughout the lifecycle of the product.
principles.detailed_description: Good design considers environmental impact throughout the product lifecycle. It conserves resources, minimizes waste, and reduces both physical and visual pollution. In digital design, this means efficient code, reduced energy consumption, accessibility of features to extend device life, and respect for users' time, attention, and data as precious resources.

Reduce digital pollution and waste

principles.name: Good design is as little design as possible
principles.original_german: Gutes Design ist so wenig Design wie möglich
principles.short_description: Less, but better. Good design concentrates on the essential aspects, and does not burden with non-essentials. Back to purity, back to simplicity.
principles.detailed_description: Good design embraces minimalism and restraint. It concentrates on what is essential and eliminates everything else. This is not about arbitrary removal but about distilling to the essence - removing non-essentials allows the essential to shine. The principle is 'less, but better' - fewer elements of higher quality and purpose.

Remove non-essential elements deliberately
Embrace restraint and minimalism with purpose
Distill to essence rather than add decoration

common_violations.impact: Visual noise obscures content and purpose

philosophy.overview: Rams' principles emphasize restraint, honesty, and user-centered simplicity. They argue for design that serves users rather than designers, that is timeless rather than trendy, and that achieves beauty through reduction rather than addition.
philosophy.design_approach: Start with user needs, add only what is essential, refine every detail, and continuously ask what can be removed without losing value.
